newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia cash, short-term reserves rise in H1.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia cash, short-term reserves rise in H1.

text.p: Cash and short-term reserves in Mongolian banks rose in the first half of 1997 to 18 billion tugriks ($22.56 million) from 10 billion tugriks at the start of the year, the Bank of Mongolia said on Wednesday.
"The liquidity position of banks has sharply improved since the beginning of the year," governor of the central bank Unenbat said in an interview.
At the end of June, banks had total cash holdings of 12 billion tugriks in the central bank and another six billion tugriks invested in central bank bills, he said.
Banks could make a 50 percent return in a year by buying the bank bills, which are auctioned to commercial banks once every two weeks, Unenbat said.
An increase in interest in the bank bills was partly due to the stability of the tugrik, he said.
The central bank on Monday set the official exchange rate at 797.99 tugriks to the dollar, up from 798.03 tugriks the previous Monday. The tugrik has been relatively stable for two months.
"We expect the tugrik to be stable in the future," Unenbat said. "There will only be insignificant fluctuations, which will be easily managed by the central bank."
The central bank calculates the official rate based on the previous week's interbank trade.
